props.title: Good Boys
props.initialSlug: Growing up is a wild adventure.

sections.content: **Good Boys (2019)** (2019) revolutionized the coming-of-age comedy by bringing raw tween authenticity to the R-rated space. Following **Superbad** (2007)'s DNA but aging down the protagonists, it captured that precise moment when kids start questioning childhood while still being hilariously naive. The film's genius lies in how it handles innocence - these 12-year-olds misunderstand adult objects and concepts in ways that feel genuine rather than purely played for laughs. It's spiritually connected to **Stand By Me** (1986), sharing that film's understanding of how kids actually talk and behave when adults aren't around.

sections.content: The success of **Good Boys** (2019) sparked a mini-renaissance of R-rated coming-of-age films that don't sanitize the awkwardness of early adolescence. **Little Women** (2019) and **Lady Bird** (2017) proved you could tell sophisticated stories about young people without talking down to the audience. These films share an understanding that kids are complex characters capable of carrying meaningful narratives while still being fundamentally kids.

The film's treatment of friendship deserves special attention, following in the footsteps of classics like **The Sandlot** (1993) and **Now and Then** (1995). The core relationship between Max, Thor, and Lucas feels lived-in and real, capturing that specific age when best friends are everything and growing apart seems impossible. It's reminiscent of how **The Way Way Back** (2013) and **Kings of Summer** (2013) portrayed teenage friendship as both salvation and complication. SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Coming-of-Age Comedy

sections.content: Where teen comedies like **American Pie** (1999) played exclusively for shock value, **Good Boys** (2019) finds its humor in genuine character moments. It shares more DNA with **School of Rock** (2003) and **Hunt for the Wilderpeople** (2016) in how it respects its young characters while finding humor in their perspective on the adult world. The film proves you can be both raunchy and sweet, following the path blazed by **The Florida Project** (2017) in showing childhood with unvarnished honesty.
